title: Meeting and playing with New Orleans musicians; banjo lessons with George Guesnon
summary: He wanted to meet musicians in person; sat in with several bands, befriended Guesnon, heard Kimball; it exceeded expectations.

bands.name: Billie and De De Pierce's band

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Well, we wanted to first look at the whole thing from the city and the musicians, from whom we've been listening to years, we've listened to the books, and read books.
And that you wanted to see all of them personally?
Yes. I wanted to see all of them personally and hear them.
Have you known many musicians here? Yes.

I also had the opportunity to play with a few of them. So Punch Millers Band, Billy & Dee Dee, and Kit Howard's Band, and Sweet Emmas Band. And we were very friends with George Gaynor, the Band-Jus-Spieler. We were looking for him right now, as we came here, to take him to take a degree. My wife wanted to take a degree. And his knowledge was done. And that went well. He was very good. He was very happy, that he had from far away a lot of students. There were many of him already, from England and Germany. And he was a very nice person. And we learned a lot from him.
Have you heard Marvin Kimberl in Old Absent House?
Yes, I heard him at the afternoon. And the band was very good. Have you ever heard your expectations?
No. Have you ever heard your expectations? Or is it so, as you hoped it would have been? No.

It was more than I hoped. And it's of course different, if you can see the music and the music and the music and hear them and play them, than if you can hear them just on plates. It's definitely something different. You can experience it more with them, if you can sit there and hear them and see them.
